active_paradigms.idea: Gradient-based continuous refinement via scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) over all centers and radii jointly
active_paradigms.description: Treat the packing as a smooth constrained optimization: variables are the 78 coordinates plus 26 radii (104 total). Objective: maximize sum(r) (minimize -sum r). Constraints: for each pair (i,j), sqrt((xi-xj)^2+(yi-yj)^2) - ri - rj >= 0, and border constraints ri - xi <= 0, ri + xi - 1 <= 0, etc. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with method 'SLSQP' or 'trust-constr', providing analytic Jacobians (pairwise distance derivatives are trivial). Initialize from the current best known configuration (the hex-row layout with greedy radii, sum ~2.542) and from several perturbed variants. This directly refines a near-optimal KKT point rather than doing discrete local moves, and can push circles off the lattice continuously to exploit corner slack that greedy discrete moves miss. Run 10-20 restarts within the 350s budget, keeping the best valid result, and apply a final feasibility-repair scaling (the existing _scale_safe) to guarantee strict validity.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii (primary score) by continuous local refinement of an already-good packing
active_paradigms.cautions: Constraints must be smooth and vectorized to stay within timeout; use the existing greedy assignment as the initializer; run several restarts from perturbed hex layouts and keep the best; verify final validity with the evaluator's tolerance (1e-6) by adding a tiny safety margin to constraints.

active_paradigms.idea: Voronoi/Laguerre (power diagram) fixed-point iteration with maximal inscribed circle radii
active_paradigms.description: Use a Lloyd-style fixed-point scheme in radius space: given current radii, place each circle at the incenter of its feasible region; given centers, set each radius to the inradius of its cell. Concretely, compute scipy.spatial.Voronoi of the 26 centers augmented with mirror sites across all four walls (so boundary cells are properly clipped by the square edges). For each cell, the maximal inscribed circle is found via a small LP or via scipy.optimize.linprog on the distance-to-halfplane-constraints problem: maximize r subject to r <= distance from (x,y) to each cell edge and to each square wall. Update each center to that incenter, recompute radii, and iterate to convergence (~50-100 iterations, each cheap). This naturally produces the optimal 'apollonian-like' packing where every circle touches at least three constraints (walls or neighbors), which is a necessary condition for optimality. Initialize from the current hex-row layout and from a few random configurations, keep the best.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii via structural optimality (every circle tangent to 3+ constraints) instead of greedy assignment
active_paradigms.cautions: Must include mirrored sites so Voronoi cells near the square boundary are clipped correctly by the true walls, not by mirror cells; corner circles need special handling (a corner cell's inradius is distance to diagonal, so cap by distance to nearest corner along diagonal); iterate until centers converge; validate with _scale_safe before returning.

active_paradigms.idea: Tangency-graph-based exact construction: solve the packing as a linear program over a fixed contact topology
active_paradigms.description: Exploit the fact that at a (locally) optimal packing, the active constraints form a tangent graph: each circle touches some walls and neighbors. Fix the combinatorial structure (which pairs are tangent, which circles touch which walls) from the current best solution or from candidate hex layouts, then solve for the exact geometry: radii and positions satisfy r_i + r_j = d_ij for tangent pairs and r_i = distance-to-wall for wall contacts. This system can be solved as a linear program: maximize sum(r_i) subject to linearized tangency constraints (for tangent pairs, d_ij >= r_i + r_j is nonlinear, but with fixed tangency directions/angles it becomes linear in positions and radii — a classic 'circle packing by LP relaxation' technique). Use scipy.optimize.linprog with variables (x_i, y_i, r_i) and constraints r_i + r_j <= ||p_i - p_j|| replaced by the linear constraints along the known contact normals from the initial layout. Iterate: solve LP, recompute exact contact normals, re-solve. This yields exact saturated packings (every circle at maximal radius given the structure) that greedy/water-filling cannot reach because they never move centers to make room simultaneously.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: sum_radii by exactly saturating a chosen contact structure (complementary slackness at optimum)
active_paradigms.cautions: The LP is only a local relaxation — feasibility of the LP does not guarantee a valid packing, so always verify with _scale_safe and only accept strictly valid improvements; degenerate/parallel tangent constraints can make the LP unbounded or infeasible, so bound all radii by 0.5; enumerate tangency patterns from the current best solution rather than random patterns to keep the search tractable within 350s.
